slot.brief: For a quadratic or cubic restricted to an interval, decide the largest interval on which it is bijective/invertible using monotonicity.

stem: For $f(x)=\dfrac{x^3-4x^2+x+6}{x-2}$ on $D=[-4,6]\setminus\{2\}$, which is the longest interval in $D$ on which $f$ is one-to-one?

verdicts.working: Factor the numerator: f(x)=x^2-2x-3 for x≠2. This quadratic is strictly decreasing on [-4,1], giving an interval of length 5. The right-hand domain component has length 4, so [-4,1] is longest.
issues: Option (C), [2,6], includes x=2, which is excluded from the stated domain.

working:
$f(x)=x^2-2x-3$ for $x\ne2$; $f'(x)=2(x-1)$. Decreasing on $[-4,1]$ (length $5$); increasing on $[1,2)$ (length $1$) and $[2,6]$ (length $4$).
